a more reactive metal corrodes instead of iron

questions.q: Why is oil used on a bike chain instead of paint?
questions.a: The chain moves and bends, so paint would crack; oil keeps coating it

questions.q: Which metal is used to galvanise iron?
Why must the sacrificial metal be more reactive than iron?
questions.a: So it reacts (corrodes) instead of the iron

questions.q: Core: Look at your rust jars (day 4). Record results and write a conclusion. Then choose a rust-prevention method for a garden gate, a ship and a bicycle chain, with reasons.
questions.a: Tap and salt water nails rusted (salt most); dry nail did not; sensible methods with reasons

questions.q: Extend: Explain why painting is a barrier method but galvanising is both barrier and sacrificial.
questions.a: Paint only blocks; zinc blocks and also corrodes first if scratched

questions.q: Stretch: Magnesium blocks protect underground pipes. Explain why they must be replaced.
questions.a: They corrode away over time as they are sacrificed

questions.q: Why does galvanised iron not rust even when scratched?
options: Zinc is more reactive and corrodes first
questions.a: B) Zinc is more reactive and corrodes first. Zinc gives sacrificial protection.

questions.q: Big question: why paint bridges again and again?
questions.a: Paint wears and chips; then water and oxygen reach the steel.

blocks.answers: Bike chain: oil or grease (moving parts); garden gate: paint; car body: paint (and galvanising); food tin: tin plating (coating).
